/-!
# Goodman's conjecture

Goodman's conjecture (1948) on the coefficients of multivalent ($p$-valent) functions in the
unit disc. Let
$$f(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$$
be analytic and $p$-valent in the unit disc, i.e. $f$ takes no value more than $p$ times there.
The conjecture claims that for every $n \geq p + 1$,
$$|b_n| \leq \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}\,|b_k|.$$
For $p = 1$ this is the Bieberbach conjecture $|b_n| \leq n |b_1|$ (de Branges' theorem).

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Goodman's conjecture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodman%27s_conjecture)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [Go48] Goodman, A. W. "On some determinants related to $p$-valent functions."
  Trans. Amer. Math. Soc. 63 (1948), 175–192.
  [doi:10.1090/S0002-9947-1948-0023910-X](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9947-1948-0023910-X)
- [LS78] Lyzzaik, A., Styer, D. "Goodman's conjecture and the coefficients of univalent
  functions." Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. 69 (1978), 111–114.
  [doi:10.1090/S0002-9939-1978-0460619-7](https://doi.org/10.1090/S0002-9939-1978-0460619-7)
- [Gr97] Grinshpan, A. Z. "On the Goodman conjecture and related functions of several complex
  variables." Algebra i Analiz 9 (1997), no. 3, 198–204.
- [Gr02] Grinshpan, A. Z. "Logarithmic Geometry, Exponentiation, and Coefficient Bounds in the
  Theory of Univalent Functions and Nonoverlapping Domains." Handbook of Complex Analysis:
  Geometric Function Theory, Vol. 1 (2002), 273–332.
  [doi:10.1016/S1874-5709(02)80012-9](https://doi.org/10.1016/S1874-5709(02)80012-9)
-/

blocks.code:
def IsPValentOn {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (p : ℕ) (s : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, {z ∈ s | f z = w}.encard ≤ p
blocks.docstring:
A function `f` is **`p`-valent on `s`** if it takes no value more than `p` times on `s`, i.e.
for every `w` the equation `f z = w` has at most `p` solutions `z ∈ s`.

Solutions are counted as points, not with multiplicity. For a function that is analytic on an
open set `s ⊆ ℂ` this agrees with the classical definition in which the roots of `f z = w` are
counted with multiplicity: a root of multiplicity `m` splits into `m` distinct simple roots of
`f z = w'` for `w' ≠ w` close to `w`. Constant functions are not `p`-valent on an open set for
any `p`, under either convention.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Set.InjOn (only the p = 1 case), Set.encard / Set.ncard of preimages (ncard rejected because it returns 0 on infinite fibers, which would make constants p-valent), Set.encard_preimage_of_injective_subset_range.
justification.name: GoodmansConjecture.IsPValentOn
justification.why_needed: Neither Mathlib nor FormalConjecturesForMathlib has a notion of a p-valent function (a function taking no value more than p times on a set). Defined as ∀ w, {z ∈ s | f z = w}.encard ≤ p. Points are counted without multiplicity; for a function analytic on an open set this is equivalent to the classical multiplicity-counting definition (a root of multiplicity m of f z = w splits into m distinct simple roots of f z = w' for w' near w), and constant functions are correctly excluded (encard = ⊤). API lemmas: `IsPValentOn.mono`, `isPValentOn_one_iff` (1-valent ↔ InjOn); tests: `isPValentOn_id`, `not_isPValentOn_const`.

blocks.name: IsPValentOn

/-- A function `f` is **`p`-valent on `s`** if it takes no value more than `p` times on `s`, i.e.

Solutions are counted as points, not with multiplicity. For a function that is analytic on an

def IsPValentOn {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (p : ℕ) (s : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, {z ∈ s | f z = w}.encard ≤ p

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 30]
theorem IsPValentOn.mono {α β : Type*} {f : α → β} {p q : ℕ} {s : Set α} (hpq : p ≤ q)
    (hf : IsPValentOn f p s) : IsPValentOn f q s :=
  fun w => (hf w).trans (by exact_mod_cast hpq)
blocks.name: IsPValentOn.mono

    (hf : IsPValentOn f p s) : IsPValentOn f q s :=
  fun w => (hf w).trans (by exact_mod_cast hpq)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 30]
theorem isPValentOn_one_iff {α β : Type*} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
    IsPValentOn f 1 s ↔ InjOn f s := by
  simp only [IsPValentOn, Nat.cast_one, encard_le_one_iff, mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h x hx y hy hxy
    exact h (f x) x y ⟨hx, rfl⟩ ⟨hy, hxy.symm⟩
  · rintro h w a b ⟨ha, rfl⟩ ⟨hb, hab⟩
    exact h ha hb hab.symm
blocks.docstring: Being `1`-valent on `s` is the same as being injective (univalent) on `s`.

  constructor
  · intro h x hx y hy hxy
    exact h (f x) x y ⟨hx, rfl⟩ ⟨hy, hxy.symm⟩
  · rintro h w a b ⟨ha, rfl⟩ ⟨hb, hab⟩

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem not_isPValentOn_const (p : ℕ) (c : ℂ) :
    ¬ IsPValentOn (fun _ : ℂ => c) p (ball 0 1) := by
  intro h
  have hinf : {z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1 | (fun _ => c) z = c}.Infinite := by
    simp only [setOf_and, setOf_mem_eq, setOf_true, inter_univ]
    exact infinite_of_mem_nhds (0 : ℂ) (ball_mem_nhds 0 one_pos)
  have := h c
  rw [hinf.encard_eq] at this
  exact (ENat.coe_lt_top p).not_ge this
blocks.docstring:
A constant function is not `p`-valent on the unit disc for any `p`: it takes its value
infinitely often.

blocks.code:
noncomputable def goodmanCoeff (p n k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  2 * k * (n + p)! / ((p - k)! * (p + k)! * (n - p - 1)! * ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 - (k : ℝ) ^ 2))
blocks.docstring:
Goodman's coefficients
$$A_{nk}(p) = \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)},$$
meaningful for `1 ≤ k ≤ p < n`, where the natural number subtractions do not truncate and
`n ^ 2 - k ^ 2 ≠ 0`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Nat.factorial, Nat.choose, Nat.descFactorial (the formula is not a single standard binomial-type quantity, so inlining or a local def was required).
justification.name: GoodmansConjecture.goodmanCoeff
justification.why_needed: The coefficient A_{nk}(p) = 2k(n+p)!/((p-k)!(p+k)!(n-p-1)!(n²-k²)) appears in both slots; a named ℝ-valued definition keeps both statements readable and lets its correctness be tested (`goodmanCoeff_one`: A_{n1}(1) = n, recovering the Bieberbach bound; `goodmanCoeff_two_three_one`: A_{31}(2) = 5; `goodmanCoeff_two_three_two`: A_{32}(2) = 4). Factorials are computed in ℕ and cast to ℝ; the natural-number subtractions p - k and n - p - 1 never truncate under the hypotheses 1 ≤ k ≤ p < n.

blocks.name: goodmanCoeff
blocks.text:
open scoped Nat in
/-- Goodman's coefficients
$$A_{nk}(p) = \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)},$$
meaningful for `1 ≤ k ≤ p < n`, where the natural number subtractions do not truncate and
`n ^ 2 - k ^ 2 ≠ 0`. -/
noncomputable def goodmanCoeff (p n k : ℕ) : ℝ :=

blocks.code:
@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem goodmanCoeff_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : goodmanCoeff 1 n 1 = n := by
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 2 := ⟨n - 2, by omega⟩
  simp only [goodmanCoeff, Nat.sub_self, Nat.factorial_zero, Nat.cast_one, Nat.factorial_succ]
  push_cast
  have h1 : ((m : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 - 1 ^ 2 = (m + 2 + 1) * (m + 1) := by ring
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < (m.factorial : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos m
  rw [h1]
  field_simp
  ring
blocks.docstring:
For `p = 1` the coefficient `A_{n1}(1)` equals `n`, so that Goodman's bound reduces to the
Bieberbach bound `|b_n| ≤ n |b_1|`.
blocks.name: goodmanCoeff_one
blocks.text:
/-- For `p = 1` the coefficient `A_{n1}(1)` equals `n`, so that Goodman's bound reduces to the
Bieberbach bound `|b_n| ≤ n |b_1|`. -/
@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem goodmanCoeff_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : goodmanCoeff 1 n 1 = n := by
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 2 := ⟨n - 2, by omega⟩
  simp only [goodmanCoeff, Nat.sub_self, Nat.factorial_zero, Nat.cast_one, Nat.factorial_succ]
  push_cast
  have h1 : ((m : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 - 1 ^ 2 = (m + 2 + 1) * (m + 1) := by ring
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < (m.factorial : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos m
  rw [h1]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem goodmans_conjecture (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (b : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hb : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, HasSum (fun n => b n * z ^ n) (f z)) (hb₀ : b 0 = 0)
    (hf : IsPValentOn f p (ball 0 1)) (n : ℕ) (hn : p + 1 ≤ n) :
    ‖b n‖ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 p, goodmanCoeff p n k * ‖b k‖ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
**Goodman's conjecture** [Go48]. Let $p \geq 1$ and let
$f(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ be $p$-valent in the unit disc $|z| < 1$, i.e. $f$ is
analytic there and takes no value more than $p$ times. Then for every $n \geq p + 1$,
$$|b_n| \leq \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}\,|b_k|.$$

Here $f$ is encoded by its coefficient sequence `b` with `b 0 = 0` (the sum starts at $n = 1$),
the power series converging to `f z` at every point `z` of the unit disc; analyticity of `f` in
the disc follows. The range $n \geq p + 1$ is needed for $(n-p-1)!$ and $n^2 - k^2 \neq 0$ to
make sense. For $p = 1$ this is the Bieberbach bound $|b_n| \leq n |b_1|$ (de Branges).

@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem goodmans_conjecture.variants.polynomial_of_univalent_p_two_three (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p = 2 ∨ p = 3) (P : ℂ[X]) (hP : P.natDegree ≤ p) (φ : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hφ : DifferentiableOn ℂ φ (ball 0 1)) (hφ' : InjOn φ (ball 0 1)) (b : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hb : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, HasSum (fun n => b n * z ^ n) (P.eval (φ z)))
    (hb₀ : b 0 = 0) (n : ℕ) (hn : p + 1 ≤ n) :
    ‖b n‖ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 p, goodmanCoeff p n k * ‖b k‖ := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
For $p = 2$ [LS78] and $p = 3$ (Grinshpan, see [Gr97] and [Gr02]), Goodman's conjecture is
known to hold for functions of the form $f = P \circ \varphi$, where $P$ is a polynomial of degree
at most $p$ (so that $f$ is $p$-valent) and $\varphi$ is univalent, i.e. analytic and injective,
in the unit disc: if $P(\varphi(z)) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ for $|z| < 1$, then for every
$n \geq p + 1$,
$$|b_n| \leq \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}\,|b_k|.$$

claims.decomposer_note: Goodman's conjecture (1948): for every p ≥ 1 and every f(z)=∑_{n≥1} b_n z^n analytic in the unit disc and p-valent (no value taken more than p times; 'multivalued' in the list entry is a misnomer for 'multivalent'), the bound holds for all n ≥ p+1 (implicit quantifier needed so that (n-p-1)! and n²-k² ≠ 0 make sense); the sum starting at n=1 encodes the normalisation f(0)=0, and p=1 recovers the Bieberbach bound |b_n| ≤ n|b_1|; Mathlib has no p-valent notion so a local definition is needed.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state this slot equivalently and faithfully: f(z)=∑_{n≥1} b_n z^n on the open unit disc (HasSum at every point of `ball 0 1` plus `b 0 = 0`, which also forces analyticity; c04/c05/c08's extra `AnalyticOn` and c03's `HasFPowerSeriesOnBall` are equivalent), p-valence as 'every fibre in the disc has `encard ≤ p`' (equivalent to the classical multiplicity count for analytic f, and rejects constants), p ≥ 1, the implicit range n ≥ p+1, and the exact coefficient 2k(n+p)!/((p-k)!(p+k)!(n-p-1)!(n²-k²)) with ℕ factorials cast to ℝ and n²−k² in ℝ (elaboration verified; c05's ℕ-valued n²−k² is also non-truncating in range). c07 chosen as base for its generic `IsPValentOn` with API lemmas/tests and a `goodmanCoeff` definition with a proven p=1 Bieberbach-reduction test and numeric tests; I changed `p < n` to `p + 1 ≤ n` and tightened docstrings.

claims.decomposer_note: Solved special case (Lyzzaik–Styer 1978 for p=2, Grinshpan for p=3; category research solved): the same inequality for p ∈ {2,3} restricted to f = P∘φ with P a polynomial and φ univalent (injective analytic) on the unit disc, where P is implicitly of degree ≤ p (or f is additionally assumed p-valent) so that f is p-valent and the conjecture's hypothesis is met.
claims.reviewer_why: Candidates split on the implicit restriction. c03/c04/c05 take 'P arbitrary polynomial, with P∘φ assumed p-valent'; that is a strictly larger class than what Lyzzaik–Styer (p=2) and Grinshpan (p=3) proved (e.g. p=2, P=w³, φ mapping the disc into a sector of opening between 2π/3 and 4π/3 gives a 2-valent φ³ not covered), so tagging it `research solved` would over-claim. c01/c02/c06/c07/c08 take `P.natDegree ≤ p`, which makes P∘φ automatically p-valent and is exactly the class in the cited papers (degree < p follows from degree = p by perturbing P by ε(X−φ(0))^p and letting ε→0). Univalence = `DifferentiableOn ℂ` (≡ analytic on the open disc) + `InjOn`; normalisation b 0 = 0 inherited from the conjecture's f(0)=0. Took c07's declaration (shares `goodmanCoeff`), with `p + 1 ≤ n` and a docstring attributing p=3 to Grinshpan via [Gr97]/[Gr02].
claims.source_text: It's known that when $p=2,3$, the conjecture is true for functions of the form $P\circ \phi$ where $P$ is a polynomial and $\phi$ is univalent.
claims.text_span: It's known that when {\displaystyle p=2,3} , the conjecture is true for functions of the form {\displaystyle P\circ \phi } where {\displaystyle P} is a polynomial and {\displaystyle \phi } is univalent.

context: Goodman's conjecture on the coefficients of multivalent functions was proposed in complex analysis in 1948 by Adolph Winkler Goodman, an American mathematician.

decomposition_objections.text: None substantive. One remark: the Wikipedia text of the second slot says only 'P is a polynomial' with no degree restriction, whereas the notes offer two inequivalent readings (deg P ≤ p, or P arbitrary with P ∘ φ assumed p-valent). These give different classes (e.g. u + εu^100 composed with a univalent φ can be univalent for small ε). I followed the notes' primary reading deg P ≤ p, which is the class treated in Lyzzaik–Styer (1978) and Grinshpan (1997); the second reading would risk asserting an unproven statement under 'research solved'.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Goodman's conjecture

Goodman's conjecture (1948) on the coefficients of multivalent ($p$-valent) functions in the
unit disc. Let
$$f(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$$
be analytic and $p$-valent in the unit disc, i.e. $f$ takes no value more than $p$ times there.
The conjecture claims that for every $n \geq p + 1$,
$$|b_n| \leq \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}\,|b_k|.$$
For $p = 1$ this is the Bieberbach conjecture $|b_n| \leq n |b_1|$ (de Branges' theorem).

*References:*

namespace GoodmansConjecture

open Metric Polynomial Set

/-- A function `f` is **`p`-valent on `s`** if it takes no value more than `p` times on `s`, i.e.
for every `w` the equation `f z = w` has at most `p` solutions `z ∈ s`.

Solutions are counted as points, not with multiplicity. For a function that is analytic on an
open set `s ⊆ ℂ` this agrees with the classical definition in which the roots of `f z = w` are
counted with multiplicity: a root of multiplicity `m` splits into `m` distinct simple roots of
`f z = w'` for `w' ≠ w` close to `w`. Constant functions are not `p`-valent on an open set for
any `p`, under either convention. -/
def IsPValentOn {α β : Type*} (f : α → β) (p : ℕ) (s : Set α) : Prop :=
  ∀ w, {z ∈ s | f z = w}.encard ≤ p

@[category API, AMS 30]
theorem IsPValentOn.mono {α β : Type*} {f : α → β} {p q : ℕ} {s : Set α} (hpq : p ≤ q)
    (hf : IsPValentOn f p s) : IsPValentOn f q s :=
  fun w => (hf w).trans (by exact_mod_cast hpq)

/-- Being `1`-valent on `s` is the same as being injective (univalent) on `s`. -/
@[category API, AMS 30]
theorem isPValentOn_one_iff {α β : Type*} {f : α → β} {s : Set α} :
    IsPValentOn f 1 s ↔ InjOn f s := by
  simp only [IsPValentOn, Nat.cast_one, encard_le_one_iff, mem_setOf_eq]
  constructor
  · intro h x hx y hy hxy
    exact h (f x) x y ⟨hx, rfl⟩ ⟨hy, hxy.symm⟩
  · rintro h w a b ⟨ha, rfl⟩ ⟨hb, hab⟩
    exact h ha hb hab.symm

@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem isPValentOn_id {α : Type*} (s : Set α) : IsPValentOn id 1 s :=
  isPValentOn_one_iff.mpr (injOn_id s)

/-- A constant function is not `p`-valent on the unit disc for any `p`: it takes its value
infinitely often. -/
@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem not_isPValentOn_const (p : ℕ) (c : ℂ) :
    ¬ IsPValentOn (fun _ : ℂ => c) p (ball 0 1) := by
  intro h
  have hinf : {z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1 | (fun _ => c) z = c}.Infinite := by
    simp only [setOf_and, setOf_mem_eq, setOf_true, inter_univ]
    exact infinite_of_mem_nhds (0 : ℂ) (ball_mem_nhds 0 one_pos)
  have := h c
  rw [hinf.encard_eq] at this
  exact (ENat.coe_lt_top p).not_ge this

open scoped Nat in
/-- Goodman's coefficients
$$A_{nk}(p) = \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)},$$
meaningful for `1 ≤ k ≤ p < n`, where the natural number subtractions do not truncate and
`n ^ 2 - k ^ 2 ≠ 0`. -/
noncomputable def goodmanCoeff (p n k : ℕ) : ℝ :=
  2 * k * (n + p)! / ((p - k)! * (p + k)! * (n - p - 1)! * ((n : ℝ) ^ 2 - (k : ℝ) ^ 2))

/-- For `p = 1` the coefficient `A_{n1}(1)` equals `n`, so that Goodman's bound reduces to the
Bieberbach bound `|b_n| ≤ n |b_1|`. -/
@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem goodmanCoeff_one (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) : goodmanCoeff 1 n 1 = n := by
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ : ∃ m, n = m + 2 := ⟨n - 2, by omega⟩
  simp only [goodmanCoeff, Nat.sub_self, Nat.factorial_zero, Nat.cast_one, Nat.factorial_succ]
  push_cast
  have h1 : ((m : ℝ) + 2) ^ 2 - 1 ^ 2 = (m + 2 + 1) * (m + 1) := by ring
  have h2 : (0 : ℝ) < (m.factorial : ℝ) := by exact_mod_cast Nat.factorial_pos m
  rw [h1]
  field_simp
  ring

@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem goodmanCoeff_two_three_one : goodmanCoeff 2 3 1 = 5 := by
  norm_num [goodmanCoeff, Nat.factorial]

@[category test, AMS 30]
theorem goodmanCoeff_two_three_two : goodmanCoeff 2 3 2 = 4 := by
  norm_num [goodmanCoeff, Nat.factorial]

/-- **Goodman's conjecture** [Go48]. Let $p \geq 1$ and let
$f(z) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ be $p$-valent in the unit disc $|z| < 1$, i.e. $f$ is
analytic there and takes no value more than $p$ times. Then for every $n \geq p + 1$,
$$|b_n| \leq \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}\,|b_k|.$$

Here $f$ is encoded by its coefficient sequence `b` with `b 0 = 0` (the sum starts at $n = 1$),
the power series converging to `f z` at every point `z` of the unit disc; analyticity of `f` in
the disc follows. The range $n \geq p + 1$ is needed for $(n-p-1)!$ and $n^2 - k^2 \neq 0$ to
make sense. For $p = 1$ this is the Bieberbach bound $|b_n| \leq n |b_1|$ (de Branges). -/
@[category research open, AMS 30]
theorem goodmans_conjecture (p : ℕ) (hp : 1 ≤ p) (f : ℂ → ℂ) (b : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hb : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, HasSum (fun n => b n * z ^ n) (f z)) (hb₀ : b 0 = 0)
    (hf : IsPValentOn f p (ball 0 1)) (n : ℕ) (hn : p + 1 ≤ n) :
    ‖b n‖ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 p, goodmanCoeff p n k * ‖b k‖ := by
  sorry

/-- For $p = 2$ [LS78] and $p = 3$ (Grinshpan, see [Gr97] and [Gr02]), Goodman's conjecture is
known to hold for functions of the form $f = P \circ \varphi$, where $P$ is a polynomial of degree
at most $p$ (so that $f$ is $p$-valent) and $\varphi$ is univalent, i.e. analytic and injective,
in the unit disc: if $P(\varphi(z)) = \sum_{n=1}^{\infty} b_n z^n$ for $|z| < 1$, then for every
$n \geq p + 1$,
$$|b_n| \leq \sum_{k=1}^{p} \frac{2k\,(n+p)!}{(p-k)!\,(p+k)!\,(n-p-1)!\,(n^2-k^2)}\,|b_k|.$$ -/
@[category research solved, AMS 30]
theorem goodmans_conjecture.variants.polynomial_of_univalent_p_two_three (p : ℕ)
    (hp : p = 2 ∨ p = 3) (P : ℂ[X]) (hP : P.natDegree ≤ p) (φ : ℂ → ℂ)
    (hφ : DifferentiableOn ℂ φ (ball 0 1)) (hφ' : InjOn φ (ball 0 1)) (b : ℕ → ℂ)
    (hb : ∀ z ∈ ball (0 : ℂ) 1, HasSum (fun n => b n * z ^ n) (P.eval (φ z)))
    (hb₀ : b 0 = 0) (n : ℕ) (hn : p + 1 ≤ n) :
    ‖b n‖ ≤ ∑ k ∈ Finset.Icc 1 p, goodmanCoeff p n k * ‖b k‖ := by
  sorry

end GoodmansConjecture

items: p-valence is read as 'at most p-valent': f takes no value more than p times in the unit disc (Hayman's convention, as also in the decomposition notes). Goodman's own papers sometimes additionally require some value to be taken exactly p times; that stronger hypothesis was not imposed, so the formal statement covers all functions taking no value more than p times. The bound is the same expression either way.

Roots of f z = w are counted as distinct points (Set.encard of the fiber over the disc), not with multiplicity. For analytic f on the open disc this is equivalent to counting with multiplicity (argument principle / Hurwitz), so no strength is lost or gained. Constant functions have infinite fibers and so are not p-valent, matching the classical convention; the bound would be trivially true for them anyway.
The domain is the open unit disc `Metric.ball (0 : ℂ) 1`, implicit in the Wikipedia formulation and explicit in Goodman (1948) (|z| < 1).

The inequality is asserted for all n > p (hn : p < n); for n ≤ p the expression (n-p-1)! and the factor 1/(n²-k²) at k = n are undefined, and Goodman's conjecture is for n > p. Under 1 ≤ k ≤ p < n the natural-number subtractions p - k and n - p - 1 in `goodmanCoeff` do not truncate.

f(z) = ∑_{n≥1} b_n z^n is encoded as (hb : ∀ z ∈ ball 0 1, HasSum (fun n => b n * z ^ n) (f z)) together with (hb₀ : b 0 = 0). This is equivalent to f being holomorphic on the disc with f 0 = 0 and b its Taylor coefficients (Complex.hasSum_taylorSeries_on_ball gives one direction; a convergent power series is analytic for the other), and avoids the total function `iteratedDeriv`.
The hypothesis hp : 1 ≤ p is included following the notes (p ≥ 1); for p = 0 the p-valence hypothesis is unsatisfiable on the nonempty disc so the statement would be vacuous anyway.
|b_n| is `‖b n‖` (complex absolute value); the coefficients A_{nk}(p) live in ℝ and the sum ranges over `Finset.Icc 1 p`.

Variant: 'P is a polynomial' is formalized as P : ℂ[X] with P.natDegree ≤ p, following the notes' primary reading ('P implicitly of degree ≤ p'), which makes P ∘ φ automatically p-valent and matches what Lyzzaik–Styer (p = 2) and Grinshpan (p = 3) proved (their proofs for degree exactly p extend to degree ≤ p by continuity in the coefficients of P). The alternative reading (P of arbitrary degree with P ∘ φ assumed p-valent) is a strictly larger class not covered by those papers, so it was not used to avoid over-claiming a solved result. Constant P (degree 0) is included; then P ∘ φ ≡ 0 on the disc by b 0 = 0 and the inequality is trivially true.

Variant: 'φ univalent' is formalized as DifferentiableOn ℂ φ (ball 0 1) (holomorphic on the disc) together with InjOn φ (ball 0 1); no normalisation φ(0) = 0, φ'(0) = 1 is imposed. The normalisation b 0 = 0 (i.e. P(φ(0)) = 0) is kept from the conjecture's 'sum from n = 1'; it is without loss of generality since adding a constant to f does not change p-valence or the coefficients b_1, b_2, ….
Variant: p ∈ {2, 3} is encoded as hp : p = 2 ∨ p = 3 with a single declaration, as required by the decomposition table.

reviewer_notes: Conventions fixed by the decomposition and followed: 'multivalued' read as 'multivalent'/p-valent; p-valent in the inclusive Hayman/Goodman sense (no value taken more than p times), which is also the only sense compatible with the deg P ≤ p variant; fibres counted as distinct points (equivalent to multiplicity counting for analytic functions on an open set, as argued in the definition docstring). The main slot is robust across all candidates. For the variant, I rejected the 'arbitrary P with P∘φ assumed p-valent' reading (c03, c04, c05) because it asserts as solved a class of functions the cited papers do not cover; the shipped `natDegree ≤ p` reading matches the literature (degree < p via a limiting argument). Residual uncertainty: exact scope of Grinshpan's p=3 result (degree exactly 3 vs ≤ 3 — harmless by the limiting argument) and whether Goodman's original convention was 'exactly p-valent'; the Wikipedia source and the decomposition notes use the inclusive convention. Final file compiles with only the two expected 'declaration uses sorry' warnings; all API/test lemmas are proved.
